pain: Missed and after-hours calls ("I'm on a roof, I can't answer")
evidence: Avg shop misses ~27% of inbound calls, 35%+ in peak; 2-5 person shops miss 55-65% (CallJolt). 85% of voicemail callers never call back. Each missed call = $300-$1,200 ticket or an $8K-15K replacement lead. $45K-$120K/yr lost per $0.5-2M shop (vendor-sourced).
what_ann_fixes: Call-handling rules and coverage, missed-call text-back, CSR booking script (trained CSRs book ~90% vs 42% untrained), booking that lands on the schedule in Housecall Pro / Jobber / ServiceTitan.
offer: Leak Check finds it (free) -> Ops Audit ($2,500) -> Systems + AI Enablement ($4,500 + $750/mo)
price_anchor: One recovered install (~$10K ticket) pays for the whole setup.
hook: "What happens to a call at 7pm on a Friday at your shop? Most owners I check are losing 10 calls a week they never knew about."

pain: Estimates never followed up; change orders never billed ("We did the work, we just never wrote it up")
evidence: Residential close rates run 38-45% vs 55-65% for top shops; ~70% of quoted work walks. Most shops follow up once or never; 80% of sales need 5+ touches. SMS follow-up gets 45-55% response vs 20-30% for calls. 'If unpaid changes occur in a tight market, it can eliminate any profit' (Mike Holt forum).
what_ann_fixes: Estimate pipeline inside the software they already pay for, 4-touch follow-up (day 1/3/7/14) drafted by AI and approved by a human, written change-order rule ('no signature, no change'), job-by-job profitability in QuickBooks.
price_anchor: A 10-point close-rate lift is worth ~$28K/month to a mid-size shop (Hatch, vendor-sourced).
hook: "You quoted $80K last month and closed $24K. Who called the other $56K back?"

pain: Owner is the bottleneck; spouse does the books; software bought but not implemented ("I'm paying for a database I will never use")
evidence: 61% of HVAC shops have field-service software but ServiceTitan's Sept 2026 report says the shift is 'from adoption to implementation'. 47% of trade contractors still estimate on paper/spreadsheets. 'The integration with QuickBooks is a daily challenge' (Housecall Pro reviews). Duplicate customers are the #1 HCP-to-QuickBooks sync failure.
what_ann_fixes: Exactly the FMBS rebuild: right managers over the right parts of the business, roles written down, Housecall Pro / Jobber / ServiceTitan configured and actually used, QuickBooks sync cleaned up, purchase orders and inventory, permit/inspection tracker, SOPs and training so the owner can leave the phone.
offer: Ops Audit & Roadmap ($2,500, 3 weeks) -> Systems + AI Enablement ($4,500 + $750/mo) -> optional fractional ops retainer ($3,000/mo)
price_anchor: Fractional COO firms charge $3K-$6K/mo virtual; Nexstar-type coaching $1.2K-$4.8K/mo with no implementation. She is local, on-site, and builds it.
hook: "Two years ago FMBS in Pompano was three companies merging with no system. We put managers in the right seats and built booking, permits and inventory. They hit their five-year numbers in two."

pain: Can't hire or keep techs; new hires take months to be billable ("Can't find good help")
evidence: 52% of contractors cite skilled-labor shortage as the top headwind; 86% say lack of qualified candidates is the biggest hiring problem. Tech turnover 20-35%/yr; replacement cost $15-25K; 6-12 months to full productivity. PE platforms (Wrench/Lindstrom, Seacoast, Apex) outbid independents and push quota culture; Air Pros USA went Chapter 11 in March 2025.
what_ann_fixes: Onboarding path and ride-along curriculum, written SOPs, pay bands and career ladder, manager coaching (the FMBS hiring/training work), plus grant-funded half-day workshops for the office and techs.
offer: Ops Audit ($2,500) -> Team Training: Frontline $500/person, Managers $750/person; CareerSource Broward reimburses up to 90% of the training line
price_anchor: 15-person frontline cohort = $7,500, company pays ~$750 after the Broward grant. Only the training line is grant-eligible; keep it invoiced separately and under $10,000.
hook: "You can't hire another tech this quarter. But I can get the ones you have 20% more billable hours and get Broward to pay 90% of the training."

pain: Marketing agency burn and weak web presence ("Last guy took $15K and I got nothing")
evidence: 91% of homeowners check reviews first; 68% only use 4+ star businesses; the Map 3-pack takes 44% of local clicks. Angi leads $25-75 shared 3-8 ways; LSA $50-120/lead in Miami/Palm Beach; 69% say lead quality fell in 2025. 'Out of over 20 leads only 1 person actually submitted the request' (Trustpilot). Bee Cool: agency counting existing customers as new leads; a prior agency's AI misuse got them delisted from Google for two months.
what_ann_fixes: Website that books (widget tied to their software), reviews on the site, review-request engine after every job, maintenance-plan page, real photos/video of the crew, honest reporting, agency replaced or held to a number.
offer: Marketing & Website Makeover ($3,500 + media) or New Service & Website Launch (Bee Cool Phase 3)
price_anchor: Contractor sites run $5K-$12K custom; agencies $1K-$3K/mo. She fixes the leak first so leads stop dying on the phone.
hook: "Your competitor two miles away has 400 reviews to your 60 and answers every one. That is most of why they outrank you on Maps."

pain: Florida compliance exposure: license number missing from website, Google profile, social, trucks
evidence: F.S. 489.119(5)(b): the CAC number must appear in every advertisement 'regardless of medium' and on vehicles. First offense = notice of noncompliance, 30 days to cure, then citation (~$100-$500); repeat matters go to DBPR complaint. Bee Cool's site was missing it.
what_ann_fixes: Free 15-minute License & Listing Scan: website, Google Business Profile, social, trucks checked; one-page fix list. Instant credibility: the owner can verify the finding in 30 seconds.
offer: Free scan (door-opener) -> Marketing & Website Makeover or bundled into the Ops Audit
price_anchor: Costs nothing to deliver; most 2-15 truck shops fail it.
hook: "Before I called I looked at your site. Your CAC number isn't on it, and in Florida that's a 489.119 citation waiting to happen. I'll send you the one-page fix list either way."

pain: Shoulder-season cash crunch; thin maintenance-agreement base ("Shoulder season is a liquidity crisis")
evidence: 40% of HVAC owners name cash flow their top challenge; spring/fall volume drops 30-40% with flat overhead. Benchmark maintenance agreements at 20-30% of revenue at 40-60% gross margin. Minimum wage hits $15 on Sept 30, 2026; equipment up 15-25% in 2026; A2L tooling $2-5K per truck.
what_ann_fixes: Maintenance-plan program design, tech pitch and renewal process, customer-list reactivation campaigns (AI-drafted, human-sent), 12-month operating targets and the 5-year plan.
offer: Ops Audit & Roadmap ($2,500) -> Systems + AI Enablement ($4,500 + $750/mo); Strategic Planning Day ($4,000) after the first quarter
price_anchor: Maintenance agreements are the single biggest valuation and seasonality lever and need no new software spend.
hook: "Calls drop 40% in shoulder season but your overhead doesn't. Your customer list is the cheapest revenue you own; nobody is writing to it."

pain: Permits, inspections and parts runs eating crew-days ("Parts runs are killing me")
evidence: AC change-outs need permits in all three counties; Palm Beach residential permits run 2-4 weeks. Broward approved private-provider virtual inspections (Aug 2025); Inspected-type services clear permits by photo/Zoom from ~$149. Owners describe 2-3 unrecoverable hours per parts run; 'can't sell from an empty wagon' (Heating Help forum).
what_ann_fixes: Permit/inspection tracker across jurisdictions, private-provider workflow, submittal checklists, purchase-order system and truck stock lists (the FMBS permits and inventory build).
price_anchor: One idle crew-day a week is a truck's worth of payroll with no revenue.
hook: "How many hours a week do your trucks spend at the supply house or waiting on an inspector? FMBS cut that with a PO system and a permit tracker."
